# logfire_gateway_optimization_rule (Resource)

Manages an AI Gateway optimization rule and the endpoints it applies to.

~> **Beta:** this resource is backed by a Logfire API in Beta. Its schema and behavior may change in future releases.

Requires Growth, Enterprise Cloud, or self-hosted and a token with organization:read_gateway and organization:write_gateway scopes (organization:read and organization:write are also accepted). The resource manages user rules and rules installed from the Logfire catalog. On a catalog rule (`source` is `builtin`), only `enabled` and `targets` can change. Keep every other argument equal to the value that Logfire stores. Import accepts the rule UUID or its organization-unique name.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "logfire_gateway_optimization_rule" "concise_support" {
  name        = "Concise support answers"
  description = "Keep answers on the support endpoint short."
  category    = "verbosity"
  instruction = "Answer in at most three sentences unless the user asks for detail."

  targets = [
    {
      endpoint_slug = logfire_gateway_endpoint.default.slug
    },
    {
      endpoint_slug = logfire_gateway_endpoint.default.slug
      model_pattern = "^gpt-5"
      agent_name    = "support-triage"
    },
  ]
}
```

## Targets

`targets` is the complete set of request selectors that the rule applies to.
Each target names an endpoint by slug. It can also narrow the match by model,
agent name, or system prompt. A rule without targets applies to no request.
Logfire keeps a target that a change repeats, so only the added and removed
targets change.

A successful apply means that Logfire stored the rule and queued a Gateway
refresh. The Gateway applies the change when the refresh completes.

## Endpoint replacement

If an endpoint is deleted, Logfire deletes the targets that name it. Logfire
also deletes them when Terraform replaces an endpoint and keeps its slug, for
example with `terraform apply -replace` or after `terraform taint`. Terraform
plans the rule before the replacement, so it plans no change. After the apply,
the new endpoint serves requests without the rule. The next apply adds the
targets again.

To replace a `user` rule together with the endpoint in the same apply, add
`replace_triggered_by` with the `id` of each endpoint that `targets` names:

```terraform
resource "logfire_gateway_optimization_rule" "concise_support" {
  # ...

  lifecycle {
    replace_triggered_by = [logfire_gateway_endpoint.default.id]
  }
}
```

The replacement deletes the rule and then creates it again. For a short time
during the apply, the rule does not apply to any request.

Do not use `replace_triggered_by` on a catalog rule. The replacement deletes the
catalog rule and creates a `user` rule in its place. After you replace an
endpoint that a catalog rule targets, run `terraform apply` again.

## Catalog rules

A rule installed from the Logfire catalog has `source = "builtin"` and a
`template_slug`. Logfire allows only `enabled` and `targets` to change on such a
rule. After you import one, set every other argument to the value that Logfire
stores. `terraform state show` lists them. The plan fails before apply if the
configuration changes another argument.

## Patterns

Logfire checks that the Gateway can run each new `trigger_pattern` and
`system_prompt_pattern`. An invalid pattern fails the apply with a validation
error. If the Gateway cannot check a pattern, Logfire answers with a 503 and
stores nothing. Apply again later.

## Concurrent changes

If another change to the rule arrives while Logfire saves an update, Logfire
answers with a conflict and a `Retry-After` delay. The provider waits for that
delay and sends the update again, at most three times in all.

## Failed creates

Creation is not retried automatically. A failed request can still leave a rule
stored. Check the rule list before retrying. If the name exists, import the rule
by name and apply the configuration again.

## Supported configuration

The resource manages rules whose targets select an endpoint and, optionally, a
model pattern, an agent name, and a system prompt pattern. A rule that the
Logfire UI targeted at a project, a Gateway API key, a provider, or a system
prompt hash, or that has a disabled target or more than 100 targets, returns a
conflict error. Manage such a rule in the Logfire UI.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `category` (String) Catalog category of the rule. One of `prompt_hygiene`, `tool_use`, `verbosity`, `quality`, or `style`.
- `instruction` (String) Text that a `transform` rule appends to the message that `message_role` selects.
- `name` (String) Organization-unique rule name, at most 2,048 bytes in UTF-8.

### Optional

- `action` (String) `transform` appends the instruction to the request. `observe` records that the rule matched and leaves the request unchanged. Defaults to `transform`.
- `description` (String) Rule description.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the Gateway applies the rule. Defaults to `true`.
- `failure_mode` (String) What the Gateway does when it cannot evaluate the rule. `fail_open` skips the rule and serves the request. `fail_closed` refuses the request. Defaults to `fail_open`.
- `message_role` (String) Message that the instruction is appended to. `system` appends to the system prompt and creates one if the request has none. `user` appends to the final user turn, and the Gateway skips the rule for a request without one. Defaults to `system`.
- `priority` (Number) When targets are equally specific, the Gateway applies rules with a higher priority first. Defaults to 100.
- `targets` (Attributes Set) Complete set of request selectors that the rule applies to, at most 100. A change replaces the whole set. A rule without targets applies to no request. Defaults to an empty set. If an endpoint is deleted, Logfire deletes its targets, and the next plan shows the change. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--targets))
- `trigger_pattern` (String) Regular expression that the request must match for the rule to apply. Omit it to apply the rule to every matching request. Logfire checks that the Gateway can run the pattern.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when the rule was created.
- `id` (String) Rule UUID.
- `source` (String) `user` for a rule created through Terraform, the API, or the editor. `builtin` for a rule installed from the Logfire catalog.
- `template_slug` (String) Catalog template of a `builtin` rule. Null for a `user` rule.

<a id="nestedatt--targets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `targets`

Required:

- `endpoint_slug` (String) Slug of a Gateway endpoint in the same organization, for example `logfire_gateway_endpoint.default.slug`.

Optional:

- `agent_name` (String) Agent name that the request must carry. Omit it to match every agent.
- `model_pattern` (String) Regular expression that the requested model must match. Omit it to match every model.
- `system_prompt_pattern` (String) Regular expression that the system prompt must match. Omit it to match every system prompt.

## Import

Import a rule by name or UUID using the same organization's management token:

```terraform
import {
  to = logfire_gateway_optimization_rule.concise_support
  id = "Concise support answers"
}
```

Or use the command line:

```shell
# Import an existing Gateway optimization rule by its organization-unique name, or by its UUID.
#
# By name:
terraform import 'logfire_gateway_optimization_rule.concise_support' "Concise support answers"

# By UUID:
terraform import 'logfire_gateway_optimization_rule.concise_support' "018f45c0-3cab-7b2f-a8f7-8a0b55a7ee00"
```
